title: Why AI Can't Optimize a Factory It Doesn't Understand
description:
A machine stops and ERP, MES, maintenance and the PLC each know part of the story, so AI cannot safely optimize the response. This episode shows manufacturing and data leaders how semantic layers, knowledge graphs, digital twins and clear constraints give AI the factory context it needs to support real production decisions.
In this episode
00:00 – A machine stops: why AI needs factory context05:07 – Every system knows something09:50 – Data versus context14:30 – Dashboards, prediction and optimization27:50 – Knowledge graphs and digital twins41:40 – Asset identity, constraints and data quality65:50 – Architecture with Azure, Fabric and Power BI79:40 – Semantic layer, simulation and accountable decisions
Key takeaways
Factory AI fails less from weak models than from missing context: which asset, operation, order, tool, person and rule an event belongs to.A semantic layer or knowledge graph should connect facts across ERP, MES, maintenance, quality and machine data while the source systems keep ownership.Prediction, simulation, optimization and generative AI have different jobs, and a named person still approves decisions while safety and control stay in the operational layer.

Episode page: the full episode with chapters, key takeaways and an FAQ on factory AI contextMicrosoft Fabric – the shared place to combine ERP, MES, maintenance and quality data, which still lacks shared meaningMicrosoft Azure – the layer for secure event intake, integration and processing, kept outside safety and control pathsSemantic model – the fix for conflicting terms like available, complete and done across ERP, MES and qualityPower BI – the consumption end that shows OEE, downtime and impact but cannot decide what production moves nextAI assistant – the planner's helper that can only answer grounded questions once orders, assets and rules are connectedRelated episode: Microsoft Fabric Shortcuts - Simply Explained
